uncited: It solves the problem of novel view synthesis by learning a continuous radiance field parameterized by neural networks, distinct from grid-based or explicit mesh representations.

Unlike [NeRF Training Setup](13271-nerf-training-setup.md) which uses a static MLP, NLR employs a specific architecture optimized for learning light fields, and unlike [NeRF-GT Baseline Training Setup](11349-nerf-gt-baseline-training-setup.md), it focuses on the baseline performance of the original NLR formulation without meta-learning enhancements.
The method builds on the core differentiable volume rendering pipeline defined in [NeRF Training Loop](1522-training-loop-setup.md).
The source does not specify the exact internal memory layout or bit-packing of the NLR network weights or intermediate tensors.
It is noted that NLR++ variants use feature processing networks, implying a structured parameterization, but the baseline NLR structure details are not given in the sources.
**Ray Sampling:** Generate rays from camera poses as defined in the parent pipeline.
**Network Query:** Evaluate the NLR neural network at sample points along the ray to obtain volume density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$.
The specific architecture is not detailed in the provided text, but it differs from the standard NeRF MLP.
where $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$ is the accumulated transmittance and $\delta_i$ is the distance between samples.
**Loss Computation:** Calculate the photometric loss (typically Mean Squared Error) between the rendered image $\hat{\mathbf{C}}$ and the ground truth image $\mathbf{C}$.
**Optimization:** Update network parameters using gradient descent.
It learns the initialization of the shape and color networks to enable rapid specialization to new scenes.
It is chosen when few-shot novel view synthesis is required.

*   **Strengths:** Provides a baseline for neural light field representations; MetaNLR enables fast adaptation to new scenes.
